3.0.s.en: 1. A call to the leaders to know the truth:

3.0.0.en: And I said, Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel.

3.0.1.en: Is it not for you to know the truth? [1]

3.0.2.en: It was fitting for the elders of Israel to live in the midst of the people, sharing with them daily life, but they turned into a ruling aristocratic class living in the capital "Jerusalem."

3.0.3.en: And the judges, who ought to have taught the people the Law and borne witness to the divine truth, set the Law aside, and became more wicked than the people, with no work except the abuse of their positions and authority.

3.0.4.en: * Truly the prophets repeat the accusation against the people, saying: "Hear the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom... thy princes are rebellious" (Isa 1:10, 23). Again Micah says: "Is it not for you to know justice?" In fact, everywhere they restrain them (discourage them) with violence. What, then? Does anyone ascribe the fault to God? Far be it from us to have this thought. For the fault is truly in them. For what virtuous excuse could anyone offer, that you do not know the law, other than that you refuse to obey it?

3.0.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * He addresses the leaders, who were entrusted with judgment and trampled justice; therefore he put this in the form of a question: Are you not those responsible for judgment, to punish the guilty and acquit the innocent without blame? How then did those who were entrusted with the administration of the laws turn aside from practicing good and zealously support evil? You have practiced such greed with regard to the needy, stripping them of all their possessions (he suggests this by saying: you have stripped the people of their skins and the body of its bones).

3.0.6.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus We do not marvel if a simple prophet stood in a village to judge the heads and judges and to question them, for since he enjoys the divine truth he carries a special majesty, while these great men, since they did not know the truth in their life and conduct, became weak, unable to defend themselves.

3.0.7.en: Where the truth is, fear finds no place, but a man bears the fear of the Lord and in humility fears neither men nor events.

3.0.8.en: Who are those whom he questions: "Is it not for you to know the truth?" Truly they know it, and keep the Law and the statutes, perhaps by heart, but they are strangers to it in their life and conduct, and so became without knowledge.

3.1.0.en: 2 Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; 3 who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron. 4 Then shall they cry unto the LORD, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.

3.1.1.en: Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones. [2]

3.1.2.en: When the love of money and covetousness creep into the heart, a man loses his inner insight and discernment, and so hates good for others and desires evil for them.

3.1.3.en: The first mark of the oppressors is hatred of good and love of evil; they treat the poor as cannibals, holding their feasts by slaughtering the poor and cooking them.

3.1.4.en: In the Book of Ezekiel God rebukes the wicked shepherds, saying: "Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?... but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them. And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered... Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them" (Ezek 34:2, 4, 10).

3.2.0.en: Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron. [3]

3.2.1.en: It was fitting for the spiritual leaders to give themselves for the sake of the people, not to satisfy their desires and prey upon the people like savage beasts, like eaters of human flesh.

3.2.2.en: He presents a hideous picture of the brutality that these leaders reached against the people, for they eat their flesh like beasts of prey, and flay their skins so as to leave no trace of their flesh, and break their bones to eat the marrow, and chop them in pieces as for the pot, as though they were cutting up their flesh and putting it in a pot! A most painful picture of their gluttony and their cruelty without limit!

3.3.0.en: Then shall they cry unto the LORD, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings. [4]

3.3.1.en: God will not hear the cries of him who eats his brother's flesh, however much they increase and however high they rise, but the Lord hides His face from them to let justice take its course at the appointed time. "For judgment is without mercy" (Jas 2:13). As they did not listen to the cries of their brothers when they were in ease and prosperity, they too cry out in their distress and find no answer. And as they hid their faces from their poor brothers, God hides His face from them. As Adoni-bezek said: "Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me" (Judg 1:7). And the psalmist says: "With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful; with an upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright; with the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself froward. For thou wilt save the afflicted people; but wilt bring down high looks" (Ps 18:25-27). And Solomon the Wise says: "Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard" (Prov 21:13).

3.3.2.en: * At the moment in which I withdraw from evil, at that very moment I become worthy that You listen to my prayers.

3.3.3.en: St. Jerome * You adapt the reward, O Lord, according to the directions of the people. You supply the saints with what holiness deserves, and the innocent and those free from sin with what befits them, and the chosen and the perfect with what is perfect; but as for those who turn aside from the straight way and walk in the opposite direction, You guarantee that they will find the end of their way, which befits them.

3.4.0.en: 5 Thus saith the LORD concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. 6 "Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine; and the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them. 7 Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded: yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer of God."

3.4.1.en: Thus saith the LORD concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace!

3.4.2.en: And he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. [5]

3.4.3.en: While the false prophets bite the flesh of their brothers with their teeth like beasts of prey, they present honeyed, false words, proclaiming a false peace. These prophets are supported by the rich and those in authority, but it will not last, for war is surely coming!

3.4.4.en: Some translate "bite with their teeth" as "gnaw with their teeth"; for while they speak smooth things, proclaiming peace, they hide their lie by biting their lips with their teeth to hold back what is within them, so that no word escapes that would reveal their deceit and lying.

3.4.5.en: They are greedy, seeking to eat the flesh of others without ceasing. Their mouth is open to devour, and if anyone stops them they prepare war against him, threatening him with the harsh judgments of God. This is the work of covetousness for base gain (1 Tim 3:3; Titus 1:7).

3.4.6.en: * He (the prophet Jeremiah) says: "and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies" (Jer 20:6). For he who speaks wickedly of the sayings of God, and casts the prophetic words into the pit, prophesies, but he prophesies lies.

3.4.7.en: * He did not forbid them merely from listening to a prophet, but they listen to the words of the prophets when they present vanity (Jer 23:16). For he who hears a prophet like Moses does not hear him but hears the Lord who speaks through him. For the false prophets work vanity. Since they speak visions that are from their own hearts, they do not change the heart of the hearer, and so they work vanity.

3.4.8.en: Origen Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision.

3.4.9.en: It shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine.

3.5.0.en: And the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them. [6]

3.5.1.en: Since the false prophets ran after the love of money, they clung to the rich, walked in a spirit of hypocrisy, and justified injustice; so their minds became dark and their life turned into a night with no day, because they rejected the Sun of Righteousness. They lose all inner enlightenment, so their minds are darkened and their thoughts trouble them.

3.5.2.en: The Lord declares the helplessness of the false prophets, since they have no vision by night and no divination in the dark, and they come into a state of severe frustration, and shame and disgrace come upon them.

3.5.3.en: * "The sun shall go down" (Jer 15:9) on these prophets who lead my people astray, dwelling in darkness. "It shall be night to you, without vision, and it shall be darkness to you without dawn." For when (the unclean spirit) departs from a man, he passes through places (Mt 12:43). This happens exactly by nature. For (the Lord) returns this judgment upon the people. "Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation" (Mt 12:45). For in the days of the prophets there went out from them (the unclean spirit) which is sin itself.

3.6.0.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded: yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer of God. [7]

3.6.1.en: If anyone asked the false prophets for counsel, they offered what was within them of darkness, because they have no "answer of God."

3.6.2.en: The covering of the lips also points to their inability to prophesy, so their tongue falls silent and they cover their lips, and the people grope their way in the midst of spiritual darkness.

3.6.3.en: By covering their upper lips is meant covering the mustache, since the Hebrew word is שָׂפָם (sapham). The mustache and beard had a special esteem among the Hebrews as a sign of courage, manliness and strength. So covering the upper lip is a sign of grief and sorrow. Thus the text here means that the prophets are in grief, because God refuses to reveal Himself to them, and for this reason they cover their lips. For this reason the leper is required to cover his upper lip (Lev 13:45). The same custom occurs in Ezekiel (Ezek 24:17, 22).

3.7.s.en: 4. Micah and the power of the Spirit:

3.7.0.en: But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD, and of truth and might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin. [8]

3.7.1.en: While the false prophets will be exposed one day and put to shame, the prophet is vindicated continually through the work of the Spirit of the Almighty Lord and his holding fast to the divine truth.

3.7.2.en: Micah attributes the secret of his power to the work of the Holy Spirit in him. The Spirit of the Lord qualified him for the prophetic pastoral work, so he was filled with power, truth and courage, speaking as one who has authority. As Isaiah the prophet says: "For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed" (Isa 50:7). So he does not fear the opposition of men, even if they are men of authority!

3.7.3.en: The prophet realized his inability in himself to do this work, but the Spirit of the Lord is the secret of his power, because: "who is sufficient for these things?" (2 Cor 2:16), and as the Apostle says: "our sufficiency is of God" (2 Cor 3:5).

3.7.4.en: In contrast to the false prophets, upon whom severe frustration came, Micah was filled with the power of the divine Spirit, carrying inner strength, truth and might. He feels no weakness, nor does he lack knowledge of the truth, nor does he lose his heroic work in the Lord. It is as though he says to them: There is no basis for comparison between the false prophets and me, for "What is the chaff to the wheat?" (Jer 23:28).

3.7.5.en: Since the prophet Micah enjoyed these qualifications, he spoke boldly and declared to Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin. Men of God have sometimes been bound to reveal the sincerity of their mission and the divine abilities they enjoyed, not for boasting but for the sake of service and the building up of the Kingdom of God in this world.

3.7.6.en: In his interpretation of the Second Epistle to the Corinthians (2 Cor 11:21 ff.) St. John Chrysostom explains that the Apostle Paul did not do this in order to boast of himself, but to silence the mouths of those who wished to destroy his ministry by denying his apostleship. Chrysostom presented many examples of men of God who defended themselves for the building up of the Church and the success of the divine work. Samuel the prophet says: "Behold, here I am: witness against me before the LORD, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you" (1 Sam 12:3). And Amos the prophet says to Amaziah: "I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: and the LORD took me as I followed the flock, and the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel" (Amos 7:14 ff.), and so also the prophet Micah here.

3.8.0.en: 9 Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor the truth, and pervert all equity. 10 They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. 11 The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the LORD, and say, Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us. 12 Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.

3.8.1.en: Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor the truth, and pervert all equity. [9]

3.8.2.en: Since the prophet Micah enjoys the Spirit of the Almighty Lord, he will not lack the ability to speak boldly against the heads and judges who hate the truth and pervert all that is straight. Perhaps by perverting all equity he means the misinterpretation of the word of the Lord, so that they turn it to their own private advantage. This is also what the heretics do when they misuse certain scriptural phrases in the service of their heresies.

3.8.3.en: In his letter [19:8] St. Cyril the Great wrote about those who corrupt the truth by misusing certain phrases from the Holy Bible. He also sent with the letter a copy of the letter of St. Athanasius the Apostolic to Epicetetus, which the heretics had distorted.

3.9.0.en: They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. [10]

3.9.1.en: The leaders of the nation sought to build a prosperous city, so they were occupied with magnificent constructions and outward appearances at the expense of the poor class of the people. They care for the appearance and beauty of the city like those who seek the public good, while they break the Law and oppress the poor.

3.9.2.en: * "They build up Zion with blood" (Mic 3:10). They did not learn self-control, though they received this commandment first: "Thou shalt not kill," and were commanded to refrain from countless other things because of this, and in many various ways they were urged to keep this commandment. Yet they did not stop this evil habit, but what did they say when they saw Him? Come, let us kill Him. And what was the motive? What was the reason? What accusation, great or small, did they bring against Him? Is it because He honors you, and because He, being God, became man for your sake, and wrought countless wonders? Or because He forgave your sins? Or because He called you to the Kingdom? That you may see their great evil with their folly, and the cause of killing Him is their utter madness.

3.9.3.en: St. John Chrysostom The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the LORD, and say:

3.9.4.en: Is not the LORD among us?

3.10.0.en: None evil can come upon us! [11]

3.10.1.en: The prophet condemns the religious leaders who work as hirelings, whom the bribe seduces, and who turn aside because of the love of money. He also warns the rich and those in authority against using their resources to influence the servants of God; this is counted as a bribe! The false prophets turned into mercenaries who prophesy according to the silver offered to them, so they are occupied not with declaring the will of God but with how they may gain money. They imitated Balaam, who "loved the wages of unrighteousness" (2 Pet 2:15).

3.10.2.en: * You, O priest, are permitted to live from the altar, not to live in luxury. The mouth of the ox that treads out the corn is not muzzled. The Apostle did not abuse his liberty, but having food and raiment he was content, working night and day so as not to be chargeable to anyone (1 Thess 2:6; 2 Thess 3:8). And in his epistle he calls God to witness that he lived with dignity (1 Thess 2:10), without covetousness, in the gospel of Christ. He also affirmed, not concerning himself alone but concerning his disciples, that he sent no one to ask or take anything from the churches. But if in some epistles he expressed his pleasure and called the gifts which some sent the grace of God (2 Cor 12:17-18), he did not gather them for himself but for the poor saints of Jerusalem, who were the Jews who first believed in Christ, and whom their fathers and relatives drove out, and they lost their possessions and all their interests, which the priests of the temple and the people had ruined. Let these accept to take. But under the cover of the poor a few grew rich, and eat from vessels of gold and glass and china (precious porcelain). Would that by our wealth we might change our habit, or not allow the poor to be a cause for the attainment of wealth by the nobles...

3.10.3.en: St. Jerome All the civil and religious leaders, the heads, priests and prophets, agreed upon one thing, which is the love of money. And through their practice of worship in its formality without spirit they thought that God was in their midst protecting them from every evil. They think that these evil acts of theirs cause no harm, because they are the people of God in name. It is faith that does not work by love, which is a dead faith, resting on formalities without spirit and life.

3.10.4.en: "Is not the LORD among us?" Are we not in the city of Jerusalem, the city of God? Are not His temple and the ark of His covenant and His holy book and His priests and His daily sacrifices in our hands? Thus they misused the divine privileges offered to them for their sanctification, so they abandoned holiness and held fast to formalities.

3.10.5.en: The gifts of God to them were diverted from their purpose, so they imagined that God was in their midst as long as they had these gifts, even though they persisted in the love of the world, injustice and violence.

3.11.0.en: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest. [12]

3.11.1.en: This prophecy had its effective impact more than a century later, when the prophet Jeremiah quoted it (Jer 26:18), and it had a deep impression on Jeremiah. Its quotation led to the saving of Jeremiah's life when he was exposed to the danger of being put to death in the days of Jehoiakim.

3.11.2.en: They claimed that they were building Zion and caring for its constructions ]10[, not knowing that while they care for the streets and the magnificent buildings they are working for the ruin of the holy places.

3.11.3.en: If the leaders thought that since God was in their midst no destruction would come upon them, then because of their insistence on seizing fields God allows the destruction of Zion, so that its buildings are scattered, and turn into fields and ruins and desolation! What befalls Zion reveals what befalls the depths of these wicked ones, and what will also befall as the fruit of their insistence on evil, hiding behind the presence of Zion and the temple of the Lord as a sign of God's dwelling in their midst.

3.11.4.en: * Here also the divine Micah was unable to bear one in Zion in whom blood flows, which is interpreted to mean that Jerusalem is stained with injustice. While the heads of the house of Jacob were disgusted with justice, the priests taught for hire. The prophets prophesied for money! What does Micah say of the result of this? "Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become as a storehouse of fruit (ruined), and the mountain of the house as a wooded grove." He also lamented the lack of uprightness, so that a stalk (of plant) or a trace of grapes is rare, since the prince asks and the judge flatters (Mic 7:1-4). His language often resembled the mighty saying of David: "Save me, O Lord, for the righteous has failed" (Ps 12:1). So their good things will come to an end, for "thou hast consumed like the moth that which is desirable" (Ps 12:1).

3.11.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Some see that this prophecy was fulfilled literally at the hand of Titus, when the Romans plowed the land on which the city stood so that total ruin might be accomplished.

3.11.6.en: Let me know the truth, that I may become a leader!

3.11.7.en: * My soul trembles at hearing of the wicked leaders.

3.11.8.en: They thought that they knew the truth and defended it.

3.11.9.en: And they are far from knowing it!

3.11.10.en: You are the divine Truth; open my eyes that I may know You, let me walk in You, that I may live forever!

3.11.11.en: * Grant me to love the good and hate the evil.

3.11.12.en: Let me love the good, whatever its cost, and hate the evil, whatever its enticements!

3.11.13.en: * Let me love the good for every human being, that I may love You, O Lover of mankind!

3.11.14.en: Remove from me all covetousness, greed and selfishness; remove from me violent brutality.

3.11.16.en: Let me love and not seek to be loved.

3.11.17.en: For I love You even in those who oppose me.

3.11.18.en: * Let me show compassion to others, that You may show compassion to me.

3.11.19.en: Let me respond to the requests of others, that You may hear my voice and answer my prayers.

3.11.20.en: * Remove from me all hypocrisy, that I may go forth in the truth without flattery!

3.11.21.en: Let me please You, and not seek the approval of men.

3.11.22.en: I cling to You, and You shine upon me with Your light that I may know Your will, and be enlightened by the splendor of Your righteousness.

3.11.23.en: My whole life becomes day without night, and light without darkness, and love without hatred!

3.11.24.en: * Grant me the power of Your Holy Spirit, that I may be filled with power, truth and might.

3.11.25.en: Let me speak the truth, whatever its cost, and not flatter a rich man or one in authority!

3.11.26.en: Let me speak Your words without distortion!

3.11.27.en: * Let me worship You in spirit and truth, that formalities without spirit may not swallow me up!

3.11.28.en: Let me perceive Your indwelling and Your dwelling in me!

3.11.29.en: Then You establish the spiritual Zion, and sanctify my depths as a temple for You.
